spec.name: Reversal v25
spec.notes: Fade the last move, rebalanced often.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 2.4, annual return 12%, maximum drawdown 6%.

exhibits.summary: On the sealed period, traded as live (strict data, 10 bps, at least one bar of lag), the Sharpe ratio is -1.84 against 2.43 in research, a gap of +4.28.
The log holds 2 distinct specs; the best of 2 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.00, so the claimed 2.40 becomes 2.40 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 3.13 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean -0.02, 95th percentile 0.57).
Perturbing the 2 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.43 to as low as 1.25 (as low as 2.04 at 25%).
Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 2.43 to -0.12 (change -2.55).

charges.argument: The Sharpe ratio collapses from 2.43 to -0.12 when the signal is delayed by one bar, indicating the strategy relies on same-bar look-ahead information.

rebuttals.argument: The Sharpe ratio collapses from 2.43 to -0.12 when the signal is delayed by one bar, confirming the strategy relies on same-bar look-ahead information.

verdict.opinion: The strategy relies on same-bar look-ahead information, as evidenced by the Sharpe ratio collapsing from 2.43 to -0.12 when the signal is delayed by one bar. This indicates the strategy is not deployable with real capital.
